svg.desc: Every encoded obligation and how it is checked
svg.text: Figure 1 · The standard as code: obligations and how each is checked
23 obligations of MIL-STD-882E (2012-05-11) across 9 elements: 19 checked by a validator rule on every push, 4 by human review. Tailoring
Describe the risk management effort and its integration into SE, IPPD and program management
Identify prescribed and derived requirements; include them in specifications and flow them down
Define how risks are formally accepted by the appropriate authority with user representative concurrence
Document hazards in a closed-loop HTS with the minimum data elements
Identify hazards systematically across hardware, software, interfaces (including human), use and environment over the whole life …
Assess severity and probability for each hazard across all system modes using Tables I and II
Probability F only where the hazard is no longer present; never through doctrine, training, warning, caution or PPE
Express risk as a RAC and risk level per Table III
Use Tables I-III unless a tailored alternative, derived from them, is formally approved
Document all numerical probability definitions; record assessed risk in the HTS
Identify mitigations and estimate expected risk reduction in the HTS, applying the design order of precedence
Avoid signage, procedures, training and PPE as the only mitigation for Catastrophic or Critical hazards
Select and implement mitigations; present hazards, risk and mitigation status at technical reviews
Verify implementation and validate effectiveness of every selected mitigation by analysis, test, demonstration or inspection …
Accept risk by the appropriate authority before exposing people, equipment or environment to known hazards
User representative formally concurs before all Serious and High acceptance decisions
Document each risk acceptance decision in the HTS
Maintain the HTS through configuration control; reassess hazards on changes to interfaces, users, hardware, software, mission or …
Formally re-accept new hazards or risks found to be higher than previously assessed
Assign a software control category (Table IV) to each safety-significant software function
Derive SwCI from the SSCM (Table V); perform the LOR tasks for that SwCI
Where LOR tasks are unspecified or incomplete, document the software contribution at the Table VI risk level for PM decision
Document all software contributions to system risk in the HTS
Generated by tools/figures/standards_readme.py from standards/mil-std-882e/model.yaml, standards/tailoring/mil-std-882e.yaml and models/sysml/model/SusanooLibrary.sysml. The standard is encoded as
data for checking; no standard text is copied. Tailoring status: proposed, not approved.

g.text: Terms: 1A–4F = risk assessment code, severity 1–4 plus probability A–F (e.g. 1C) · DoD = US Department of Defense · F-nnn = system function in the item definition · HTS = hazard tracking
system (MIL-STD-882E Task 106; here safety/hazards/) · ID = identifier · IPPD = integrated product and process development · LOR = level of rigor (software safety tasks, MIL-STD-882E 4.4) ·
MIL-STD-882E = US DoD Standard Practice for System Safety (11 May 2012, base edition) · PM = program manager · PPE = personal protective equipment · R01 … = validator rule in tools/pdac (R13
= only a named human review accepts anything) · RAC = risk assessment code, severity category plus probability level (e.g. 1C) · SE = systems engineering · SSCM = software safety criticality
matrix (MIL-STD-882E Table V) · SW = software · SwCI = software criticality index (MIL-STD-882E Table V) · US = United States
